cells.tense: The feeling is here and settled, and you are with it as it is.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Take one settled feeling about someone close and give it ten quiet minutes, no task attached. Let it be complete on its own.
cells.core:
Something in you has finished a round — you can feel it, you're connected to people in a way that isn't straining toward anything. The wholeness you're carrying comes through other people: it arrives by being felt, not measured, and it's still here this week while your next move is just a possibility. A feeling like that gets closed too fast, by wanting to act on it or explain it.

So don't. The feeling is the whole thing right now. Sit with it the way you'd sit in a room you like, no task in it. When a want comes — to call, to fix, to say something — notice it and let it go. What you get from that is your footing under you again, and a connection with room in it, because nothing in the feeling is being pushed anywhere.
cells.sheetLine: A whole feeling has arrived. Let it sit.
cells.verb: the whole feeling arrives complete in the moment it lands, before it is named
cells.place: at the raw edge before anything has chosen what it will be

cells.tense: You are bracing for a feeling that has not arrived yet.
cells.act: decide what this is for before you spend it
cells.ask: Before you put any energy into it, name in one line what it is for. Then set that line down, and don't go back to check it.
cells.core:
You're pushing past a feeling that hasn't finished arriving. Something raw and full is happening, and you're already deciding what it means, where it's going, how it will end. The writing runs before the ink. That's the whole feeling going dead under a hard verdict about it.

The act is small: stop and put the thing before you in one line — what it is for — before you spend anything on it, energy or words or hope. One sentence. Keep it, then set it down. What's yours in that is a direction that came from you and matches what's actually here, and a feeling left open enough to keep going until it's done being what it is.

cells.tense: The feeling finished behind a door you are still at.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: The next time something catches your interest in the morning — anything small — follow it for five minutes without deciding whether it's worth it.
cells.core:
The feeling went through and closed on the other side of you, and you're paused where it started. You show up, you read the room, you take your time leaving. The connection is on the other side of that door, and the door hasn't moved. Nothing here is pointed at anything yet; you're at the raw edge with nothing lit.

So let one thing light without deciding what it's for. Something catches you in the morning — that's the spark. Follow it for five minutes with nothing asked of it and no verdict about whether it matters. What you get is a start that didn't have a plan attached, and a moment you're actually in while it lasts.
cells.sheetLine: The feeling closed. You're at the door.
cells.verb: the whole feeling arrives complete in the moment it lands, before it is named

cells.tense: You are already writing here, and the pen says you are not.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Do one fair thing this week where nobody can see you do it — return a small debt before it's asked, put a quiet thing right. Leave your name off it.
cells.core:
You move through your days following something private — what feels right between you and a person, what you owe and what you don't. You check it without calling it checking. The feel of what's fair runs the small cases, and you don't name it that way. You'd shrug and say you just get a sense about people.

The act is small: do one fair thing where no one sees. Pay a small debt before it's asked, put something right and leave your name off it. Note to yourself that you did it — you acted because you felt it, and now it's your line and not a mood you had. Fairness in your hands runs clear once you stop pretending it isn't running.
cells.sheetLine: What's fair in you keeps its own count. You shrug and call it a sense.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that emotional wholeness has been achieved — a Bound Completion shows one emotional cycle reaching its natural end, not a whole life completed, and the reader could reasonably say the card is only describing a single moment that closed. The asks survive being wrong because each one asks for a small act the medicine performs anyway — sitting with a settled feeling, naming a form before spending it, letting a spark start unpointed, paying a small debt — and none of them require the person to agree with the reading. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line implying the person is whole now; I've kept the cores on what this capacity is doing, this present week, in the raw moment before it picks a shape.
